reaction.episode: Active CORRECTION through the Nov 17 close: SPX is down 6.42% from its 120-day high and sitting on its 200-day (-0.05%), while SMH ($460.10) and NVDA ($155.46) have both failed below their Zone 2 floors, VIX closed at 25.46 above the 25 stand-down line, HY OAS is calm at 3.43, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4 (credit calm only). Episode data is fresh, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: SPX closes above $7,820 with SMH above $600 and HY OAS still under 4% — the correction call is wrong, the market has repaired, and the Watch stance and ladder are void; re-rate to a Probe/Add posture on the repaired tape.

ladder.response: Escalation: Tranche A stays off, no probes; new money remains 100% bills; re-rate bottom probabilities and wait for a second low that holds rather than buying the first break
ladder.trigger: SPX daily close below 7,300 (the defended bottom, under the 200-day at $7,344.53)

ladder.response: Trap case: treat as a bull trap, do not chase the first bounce and add nothing; require a close above the failure zone plus tally at 3 of 4 before any probe

ladder.response: Stand-down stays in force (VIX) or triggers (HY OAS): ladder frozen, new money 100% bills; if HY OAS breaks 4%, the rotation read is void and the posture moves toward Trim/Exit review

ladder.response: Re-entry: re-arm Tranche A probe (25% per the ladder) on the zone reclaim with tally confirmation — not on the first bounce, only on the reclaim

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the live risk: NVDA's earnings beat already rallied futures and then faded — the stock is down 2.37% at $151.35 by the early afternoon, below its morning level — which is exactly how a bull trap prints. Entries must wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — a close above SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820 with tally confirmation — not the first bounce off an oversold RSI. No chasing, no sizing into the bounce.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is active, both AI-complex zones have failed below their floors, and VIX closed at 25.46 — above the 25 stand-down line — with the mechanical tally at 1 of 4. New money stays in bills; no tranche is armed and no probe is justified on this tape.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read is the data's read, not just the narrative's — credit is not cracking, so this is leadership change rather than a confirmed broad rollover. The risk is that credit conditions can flip: if HY OAS breaks above 4% while the Mag7 gap keeps widening, the rotation thesis dies and the rollover thesis takes over. AAPL, only 2.3% off its high, is the counterweight — the unwind is not uniform even inside the Mag7.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 18.77% below their 52-week highs against SPY just 6.6% below its high — a 12.17-point divergence gap. But bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and high-yield spreads are calm at 3.43% (HY OAS), with the 2s10s curve positive at +0.29. SPX itself is down only 6.42% from its 120-day high. The weakness is concentrated in the index's heaviest names, not in credit or the broad market.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as an AI-led unwind: the Magnificent 7 are the story, with NVDA down 37.8% from its high and the AI complex in free fall, while the broad index looks comparatively calm.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% while the Mag7-SPX divergence gap widens past 15 points.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals are ahead of price across the AI stack — the businesses are still growing while the multiples compress. That is an opportunity setup, not a confirmation of a broken thesis. But the counter-read cuts both ways: NVDA's earnings beat failing to hold the stock (down 2.37% by the early afternoon after the rally headline) says the market is not yet willing to pay for the growth, and buying into a falling knife needs a zone reclaim, not a revenue print. The dislocation is real; the entry is not armed until price confirms.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits 37.8% below its high at $151.35 with an RSI of 21.2, and it fell 2.37% by the early afternoon despite the 'upbeat Nvidia earnings' headline that rallied futures. The same gap repeats across the stack: Datadog revenue +27.7% year over year while 43.9% below its high, Broadcom +55% while 28.1% below, Onto +41.5% while 48.3% below, Lam Research +131.3% while 52.3% below. MU is 44.3% below its high with an RSI of 36.5. SMH is below Zone 2 at $460.10, 12.27% under its 200-day.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: revenue vs price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is broken — circular finance, a CEO resignation, and a 31.5% SMH drawdown say the infrastructure build-out was a bubble, and the tape is pricing it accordingly.
themes.watchFor: NVDA closing back above its Zone 2 floor of $175, or SMH reclaiming $470.

themes.counterRead: The demand story (AI power) has not been refuted by any number in the input; the drawdown is a multiple compression riding the AI unwind. VST insider buying at the trough and BWXT's revenue growth argue the fundamentals are ahead of price. The caution is VST's acute-catalyst flag — something specific hit it, and the brief cannot name it from this input, so sizing waits on identifying that catalyst rather than on the insider signal alone.
themes.dataAnchor: BWXT is 51% below its high while revenue grows 18.3% year over year. VST is 33% below its high at $126.86, down 15.6% in a month, with insiders buying $1.17M at the trough. SMR is down 29.3% in a month and another 3.55% today; CCJ is down 21.67% in a month, OKLO 20.09%, GEV 12.46%. The power names fell with the AI complex, not on a power-specific failure — VST's decline reason is flagged ACUTE_CATALYST, but the revenue and insider-buying data point the other way.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power drawdown
themes.narrative: AI power demand was the second leg of the AI story, and the nuclear names have been cut in half — the market is saying the power thesis was as inflated as the chips.
themes.watchFor: VST reclaiming its 50-day (the $145.08 leg) or a named resolution of its acute catalyst.

themes.counterRead: The leverage-treasury narrative ran ahead of what the underlying supports: the wrappers (CONL, BMNR) fell roughly double the underlying coins, which is the signature of a narrative premium deflating rather than a fundamental repricing of crypto itself. That makes the wrappers a caution, not a buying opportunity — the premium that made them attractive on the way up is the same premium now unwinding. No bottom signal is present in the input: no zone, no tally, no insider or revenue anchor for these names.
themes.dataAnchor: CONL, a holding, is down 59.51% in a month and another 5.25% today. BMNR, a holding, is down 31.48% in a month and 1.41% today. Bitcoin is down 22.76% in a month and 3.24% today, Ethereum down 25.37%, Coinbase down 34.47%, Dogecoin down 25.87%. The crypto complex is the worst 1-month cohort in the tracked universe, worse than NVDA's 29.88% decline.
themes.label: Crypto leverage unwind
themes.narrative: Crypto and its leveraged wrappers were the high-beta expression of the same risk appetite, and the unwind is now the deepest in the book.
themes.watchFor: Bitcoin holding above its 200-week average or CONL's 1-month decline flattening to under 5% while BTC stabilizes.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move materializes around NVDA's post-earnings tape and today's FOMC minutes: the earnings beat already failed to hold the stock by the early afternoon, so a hawkish read on the minutes pushes SPX through its 200-day toward the defended 7,300 bottom, while a hold above the 200-day with VIX rolling under 25 re-arms the zone trade.
